summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Coastal AI's UGC summarization and multilingual search product. Key concerns: context length (32k+ for long transcripts), multilingual accuracy (esp. Spanish/Portuguese), tool-calling/function call support for retrieval and external APIs, and hosted vs dedicated vs private trade-offs (latency vs cost vs data controls). Agreed next steps: send pricing/security docs and schedule technical deep dive and benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Jillian (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining um really appreciate you taking the time. quick round-robin?
[00:07] Ravi (Coastal AI): yeah this is Ravi, I'll kick off. we're building an assistant that ingests user-generated content and long call transcripts, need better summarization and multi-lingual search, mostly en/es/pt, also some fr.
[00:18] Sofia (Coastal AI): Sofia here, CTO, mainly interested in latency/cost tradeoffs and how we keep pii out of hosted logs.
[00:25] Marco (Redwood): Marco from Redwood, I'll cover technical details and propose benchmarking. Jillian will handle pricing and next steps.
[00:33] Ethan (Coastal AI): Ethan - platform, I'll ask about VPC/SSO/KMS and deployment options.
[00:40] Jillian (Redwood): great, goal for today: understand model needs (open models vs proprietary), context length, multilingual, and whether dedicated/private is needed. then agree next steps. sound ok?
[00:48] Ravi: yep. high level - we process long recordings, often 30-90 minutes; we need summarization and chunked embeddings for search. so context windows of 32k help, but for full call stitching 100k would be great.
[01:05] Marco: right - so options: for open models you can run 32k-capable variants (Llama2-32k or newer Llama3-32k), Mistral Mixtral has some 32k flavors too, and there are 100k experimental variants but they cost more and latency rises.
[01:22] Ravi: are those supported on Redwood hosted? and how does dedicated change that?
[01:27] Marco: on hosted we expose curated model catalog with performance profiles — for Llama3-ish variants and Mistral we have vetted configs; hosted supports up to 32k broadly, 100k is usually a dedicated or private deployment where you can pin a specialized kernel and more GPU memory. hosted can fallback to chunking for longer contexts automatically but that can influence final output coherence.
[01:47] Sofia: chunking worry - we need contiguous cross-chunk summarization to preserve references. is Redwood offering prefix/KV cache stitching?
[01:55] Marco: yes we have prefix/KV caching and stitching primitives; they preserve KV cache across requests, it's not perfect, sometimes you get repetition or loss at boundaries, but with our batching and caching it's much better than naive chunking.
[02:09] Ravi: multilingual - Spanish and Portuguese quality is critical. which open models are best? we prefer open-model stack to avoid vendor lock.
[02:17] Marco: Spanish/PTL performance: Llama 3 and Mixtral are solid; Mistral family tends to be strong multi-lingual out of box. Falcon can be rougher in certain dialects. We also maintain model-specific evals; we can share performance sheets showing Rouge/BLEU-like metrics on your sample prompts.
[02:36] Jillian: we'll share the model performance matrix and our recommended quantization profiles (8-bit Q8_0, 4-bit Q4 variants) — that affects latency and cost.
[02:45] Ethan: tool-calling: we need function-calls for retrieval and triggering downstream APIs (e.g., payment service). do open models support tool-calls reliably?
[02:54] Marco: function-calling is mostly a pattern — we add a lightweight shim in the runtime that maps model outputs to structured function calls. Some models are more deterministic with JSON-like outputs; we typically recommend instruction-tuned variants. On hosted we support structured output + tool-call hooks, same interface for dedicated/private.
[03:11] Ravi: ok. any limitations with streaming? we stream tokens back, right?
[03:15] Marco: yes streaming is supported. latency depends on model size and batch coalescing; smaller quantized models stream faster. For low tail latency we suggest dedicated pools with pinned models and fewer tenants.
[03:27] Sofia: security - SOC2, KMS integration, RBAC, VPC peering — how mature is Redwood Private?
[03:35] Marco: Redwood Private is our VPC/on-prem option. supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs. We have SOC2 docs and deployment checklist — Jillian will share the security pack.
[03:47] Jillian: yes sending security-summary.pdf after this. also note: hosted does not index customer data for training, we have retention controls and optional private keys for requests, but some customers opt for Dedicated or Private for full isolation.
[04:01] Ravi: cost question - rough $/1k tokens between hosted and dedicated?
[04:05] Jillian: quick ballpark: hosted for open models (quantized) can be fairly low, dedicated is usually lower unit-cost at scale but requires committed capacity, private has platform fees on top. we'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[04:17] Ravi: for benchmarking, we want to test: 1) summarization quality on 1k/10k/30k transcripts, 2) multilingual recall, 3) function-calling reliability, 4) latency P95. can Redwood run that or do you want us to run on our infra?
[04:31] Marco: we can run joint benchmarks. typical approach: you provide sample dataset and prompts, we run on hosted + dedicated config (if you want dedicated we'd simulate with an isolated pool) and share latency/cost/quality matrices. If you prefer private we can provide the plan for on-prem run.
[04:48] Ethan: network egress - if we host in Redwood do we have control over region and data residency?
[04:54] Jillian: yes hosted has region controls; dedicated/private are stronger for residency requirements. We'll note your region preference?
[05:00] Ravi: US-East + eu-west for now.
[05:03] Marco: noted.
[05:06] Sofia: about model variants - we worry about hallucination on retrievals. is reranking recommended?
[05:12] Marco: reranking + retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) best practice. We support embeddings and re-ranker pipelines; embeddings are stored in your account and can be private. Using a small cross-encoder re-ranker can reduce hallucination.
[05:27] Ravi: any hard limits we should know about for context on hosted?
[05:31] Marco: hosted catalog mostly up to 32k for current stable models; beyond that we offer experimental 100k variants typically in Dedicated/Private. If you need 100k now we can propose a Dedicated pilot.
[05:44] Jillian: question for you - what's your expected throughput? concurrent users, qps, etc?
[05:48] Ravi: variable. peak during billing windows maybe 150 qps for embeddings and 25-40 gen qps. typical latency target p95 < 800ms for short queries, for long-context summarization we accept higher latency up to 5s.
[06:05] Marco: ok that gives sizing guidance. for 25-40 gen qps with 32k models you'd likely want a dedicated pool to keep latency stable; hosted can work for early stages.
[06:15] Ethan: onboarding timeline - we'd like a pilot in Jan. what does that look like?
[06:19] Jillian: pilot: 4-6 weeks. Steps: sign NDA/PO, share sample data, we run benchmarks, then propose committed capacity or hosted billing. We'll send standard pilot contract template.
[06:30] Ravi: compliance - data deletion requests, logs, audit history?
[06:34] Marco: we support audit logs and retention configs; for private you control retention fully. For hosted we offer configurable retention windows and can support contractual deletion.
[06:43] Sofia: any customers in our vertical? finance adjacent - user generated content and payments - who else?
[06:48] Jillian: we have clients in fintech and marketplace spaces; can share anonymized case studies.
[06:53] Ravi: ok can we get a list of recommended models for our use case (summarization + embeddings + re-ranking) and the expected token cost and latency per model?
[06:59] Marco: yes we'll produce a recommended shortlist: Llama3-32k-instr (good accuracy, decent latency), Mixtral-32k (strong multilingual), Falcon-40b-instr (fast but variable on non-en), and a 70B quantized variant if you want better quality at cost. We'll include Q4_0 and Q8_0 profiles and expected p95 numbers.
[07:18] Ethan: one more - function call reliability under load? we'd like deterministic mapping to our internal APIs.
[07:23] Marco: we can instrument that in the benchmark; we also provide a test harness that validates schema outputs and retries.
[07:29] Sofia: are there any constraints around embeddings storage encryption at rest?
[07:33] Marco: yes encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private; hosted uses our KMS but we offer bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private.
[07:44] Jillian: recap: we'll send pricing/security docs, model performance matrix, and pilot contract. Marco will schedule tech deep dive and design the benchmark. Ravi will send sample dataset. agreed?
[07:56] Ravi: yes.
[07:58] Ethan: yep.
[08:00] Jillian: perfect. putting some next steps in calendar now. thanks everyone.
[08:04] [meeting continues - technical clarifications]
[08:10] Marco: quick technical note — for 100k context variants you should expect a significant memory bump and different kernel selection, often requiring multi-gpu sharding; that's why Private/Dedicated is recommended.
[08:24] Ravi: understood. do you support auto-fallback if dedicated pool is saturated?
[08:29] Marco: yes routing policies can fallback to hosted smaller-context models or to lower-cost variants; you can configure per-route fallbacks.
[08:38] Sofia: ok let's wrap. thanks Marco. thanks Jillian.
[08:41] Jillian: thanks all. following up by EOD with docs.
[08:45] Meeting ended
